sanskrit: te nātibhṛśam abhyaghnan viśikhā jayacoditāḥ bahutvāt tu parām ārtiṃ śarāṇāṃ tāv agacchatām
english: Though the shafts, urged on toward victory, did not strike them too grievously, by their sheer multitude the two warriors were brought to the utmost anguish.

sanskrit: atha śāradvato rājan kaunteyaśarapīḍitaḥ avāsīdad rathopasthe mūrcchām abhijagāma ha
english: Then, O king, the son of Śaradvat, tormented by the arrows of Kuntī's son, sank down upon the floor of his chariot and fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: vihvalaṃ tam abhijñāya bhartāraṃ śarapīḍitam hato 'yam iti ca jñātvā sārathis tam apāvahat
english: Perceiving his master reeling and stricken by arrows, and thinking him slain, the charioteer bore him away from the field.

sanskrit: tasmin sanne mahārāja kṛpe śāradvate yudhi aśvatthāmāpy apāyāsīt pāṇḍaveyād rathāntaram
english: When Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, had collapsed in the battle, O great king, Aśvatthāman too withdrew from the Pāṇḍava to another part of the field.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śāradvataṃ pārtho mūrchitaṃ śarapīḍitam ratha eva maheṣvāsaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: Beholding the son of Śaradvat swooning, racked by arrows, the great archer Pārtha, there upon his chariot, lamented piteously.

sanskrit: paśyann idaṃ mahāprājñaḥ kṣattā rājānam uktavān kulāntakaraṇe pāpe jātamātre suyodhane
english: Beholding this, the deeply wise Vidura had spoken to the king when wicked Suyodhana, destroyer of the lineage, was but newly born:

sanskrit: nīyatāṃ paralokāya sādhv ayaṃ kulapāṃsanaḥ asmād dhi kurumukhyānāṃ mahad utpatsyate bhayam
english: 'Let this defiler of the line be sent rightly to the other world; for from him will arise a great terror for the chiefs of the Kurus.'

sanskrit: tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ vacanaṃ satyavādinaḥ tatkṛte hy adya paśyāmi śaratalpagataṃ kṛpam
english: That word of the truth-speaker has now come to pass, for on his account I see Kṛpa today laid out upon a bed of arrows.

sanskrit: dhig astu kṣātram ācāraṃ dhig astu balapauruṣam ko hi brāhmaṇam ācāryam abhidruhyeta mādṛśaḥ
english: Fie upon the warrior's code, fie upon strength and manly valor! For who like me would do violence to a brāhmaṇa, his own teacher?

sanskrit: ṛṣiputro mamācāryo droṇasya dayitaḥ sakhā eṣa śete rathopasthe madbāṇair abhipīḍitaḥ
english: My teacher, son of a seer, the beloved friend of Droṇa — here he lies upon his chariot, oppressed by my arrows.

sanskrit: akāmayānena mayā viśikhair ardito bhṛśam avāsīdad rathopasthe prāṇān pīḍayatīva me
english: Though I wished it not, sorely afflicted by my shafts he sank upon his chariot; it is as though he wrings the very life from me.

sanskrit: śarārditena hi mayā prekṣaṇīyo mahādyutiḥ pratyasto bahubhir bāṇair daśadharmagatena vai
english: For I, myself worn by arrows yet observant of the tenfold duty, have driven back with many shafts this man of splendor, lovely to behold.

sanskrit: śocayaty eṣa nipatan bhūyaḥ putravadhād dhi mām kṛpaṇaṃ svarathe sannaṃ paśya kṛṣṇa yathā gatam
english: His falling grieves me more even than the slaying of a son. See, Kṛṣṇa, how piteously he has sunk, undone, upon his own chariot.

sanskrit: upākṛtya tu vai vidyām ācāryebhyo nararṣabhāḥ prayacchantīha ye kāmān devatvam upayānti te
english: Those bulls among men who, having received learning from their teachers, render to them here the objects of their desire — they attain to godhood.

sanskrit: ye tu vidyām upādāya gurubhyaḥ puruṣādhamāḥ ghnanti tān eva durvṛttās te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: But those basest of men who, having taken learning from their elders, then slay those very ones — such evil-doers go to hell.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ narakāyādya kṛtaṃ karma mayā dhruvam ācāryaṃ śaravarṣeṇa rathe sādayatā kṛpam
english: Surely, then, this deed I have done today leads to hell — bringing low my teacher Kṛpa upon his chariot with a rain of arrows.

sanskrit: yat tat pūrvam upākurvann astraṃ mām abravīt kṛpaḥ na kathaṃ cana kauravya prahartavyaṃ gurāv iti
english: For when of old he was imparting the weapon to me, Kṛpa told me: 'In no wise, O Kaurava, is a blow ever to be struck against one's teacher.'

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vacanaṃ sādhor ācāryasya mahātmanaḥ nānuṣṭhitaṃ tam evājau viśikhair abhivarṣatā
english: That word of my good and great-souled teacher I have not heeded — raining shafts upon that very man in battle.

sanskrit: namas tasmai supūjyāya gautamāyāpalāyine dhig astu mama vārṣṇeya yo hy asmai praharāmy aham
english: Homage to that most worthy Gautama, who never flees the fight! Fie upon me, O Vārṣṇeya, who strike a blow against him!

sanskrit: tathā vilapamāne tu savyasācini taṃ prati saindhavaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rādheyaḥ samupādravat
english: While Savyasācin was thus lamenting over him, the son of Rādhā, beholding the lord of the Sindhus slain, rushed forward.

sanskrit: upāyāntaṃ tu rādheyaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārtho mahārathaḥ prahasan devakīputram idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing the son of Rādhā advancing, the great chariot-warrior Pārtha, smiling, spoke this word to the son of Devakī:

sanskrit: eṣa prayāty ādhirathiḥ sātyakeḥ syandanaṃ prati na mṛṣyati hataṃ nūnaṃ bhūriśravasam āhave
english: 'There goes the son of Adhiratha toward Sātyaki's chariot; surely he cannot bear that Bhūriśravas was slain in the fray.'

sanskrit: yatra yāty eṣa tatra tvaṃ codayāśvāñ janārdana mā somadatteḥ padavīṃ gamayet sātyakiṃ vṛṣaḥ
english: 'Wherever he goes, drive the horses thither, Janārdana, lest that bull Karṇa send Sātyaki down the road that Somadatta's son has trodden.'

sanskrit: evam ukto mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ savyasācinā pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ kālayuktam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Savyasācin, the mighty-armed Keśava of great splendor replied with this word, fitting to the hour:

sanskrit: alam eṣa mahābāhuḥ karṇāyaiko hi pāṇḍava kiṃ punar draupadeyābhyāṃ sahitaḥ sātvatarṣabhaḥ
english: 'Alone, O Pāṇḍava, this mighty-armed bull of the Sātvatas is a match enough for Karṇa — how much more so when joined by the two sons of Draupadī!'

sanskrit: na ca tāvat kṣamaḥ pārtha karṇena tava saṃgaraḥ prajvalantī maholkeva tiṣṭhaty asya hi vāsavī tvadarthaṃ pūjyamānaiṣā rakṣyate paravīrahan
english: 'And the time is not yet fit, Pārtha, for your clash with Karṇa; for Indra's weapon stands by him, blazing like a great meteor, kept and honored, O slayer of foes, that he may loose it upon you.'

sanskrit: ataḥ karṇaḥ prayātv atra sātvatasya yathā tathā ahaṃ jñāsyāmi kauravya kālam asya durātmanaḥ
english: 'Therefore let Karṇa go yonder against the Sātvata, come what may; I shall know, O Kaurava, the appointed hour of that evil-souled one.'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yo 'sau karṇena vīreṇa vārṣṇeyasya samāgamaḥ hate tu bhūriśravasi saindhave ca nipātite
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: That encounter of the Vārṣṇeya with the hero Karṇa, after Bhūriśravas was slain and the lord of the Sindhus brought down —

sanskrit: sātyakiś cāpi virathaḥ kaṃ samārūḍhavān ratham cakrarakṣau ca pāñcālyau tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And Sātyaki, his car undone, what chariot did he mount? And who were the two Pāñcāla guards of his wheels? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hanta te varṇayiṣyāmi yathāvṛttaṃ mahāraṇe śuśrūṣasva sthiro bhūtvā durācaritam ātmanaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Come then, I shall describe to you all that befell in the great battle; listen calmly, and hear of your own misconduct.

sanskrit: pūrvam eva hi kṛṣṇasya manogatam idaṃ prabho vijetavyo yathā vīraḥ sātyakir yūpaketunā
english: For long before, O lord, this was in Kṛṣṇa's mind: that the hero Sātyaki was to be vanquished by Karṇa, whose banner bears the sacrificial post.

sanskrit: atītānāgataṃ rājan sa hi vetti janārdanaḥ ataḥ sūtaṃ samāhūya dārukaṃ saṃdideśa ha ratho me yujyatāṃ kālyam iti rājan mahābalaḥ
english: For Janārdana, O king, knows past and future; therefore, summoning his charioteer Dāruka, that mighty one gave command: 'Let my chariot be yoked betimes.'

sanskrit: na hi devā na gandharvā na yakṣoragarākṣasāḥ mānavā vā vijetāraḥ kṛṣṇayoḥ santi ke cana
english: For neither gods nor gandharvas, nor yakṣas, serpents, or rākṣasas, nor any men whatsoever, are there to vanquish the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: pitāmahapurogāś ca devāḥ siddhāś ca taṃ viduḥ tayoḥ prabhāvam atulaṃ śṛṇu yuddhaṃ ca tad yathā
english: The gods, with the Grandsire at their head, and the siddhas, know this. Hear now of the matchless might of those two, and how that battle went.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ virathaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ cābhyudyatāyudham dadhmau śaṅkhaṃ mahāvegam ārṣabheṇātha mādhavaḥ
english: Seeing Sātyaki bereft of his car and Karṇa with weapon upraised, Mādhava blew a mighty blast upon his ox-strong conch.

sanskrit: dāruko 'vetya saṃdeśaṃ śrutvā śaṅkhasya ca svanam ratham anvānayat tasmai suparṇocchritaketanam
english: Dāruka, knowing the command and hearing the conch's note, brought up for him the chariot whose ensign of Garuḍa was raised on high.

sanskrit: sa keśavasyānumate rathaṃ dārukasaṃyutam āruroha śineḥ pautro jvalanādityasaṃnibham
english: With Keśava's leave, the grandson of Śini mounted that chariot driven by Dāruka, radiant as fire and the sun.

sanskrit: kāmagaiḥ sainyasugrīvameghapuṣpabalāhakaiḥ hayodagrair mahāvegair hemabhāṇḍavibhūṣitaiḥ
english: It was drawn by the steeds Sainya, Sugrīva, Meghapuṣpa, and Balāhaka — coursers that go where they will, towering, of great speed, adorned with trappings of gold.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ samāruhya ca taṃ vimānapratimaṃ ratham abhyadravata rādheyaṃ pravapan sāyakān bahūn
english: Mounting that well-yoked chariot, like a celestial car, he rushed upon the son of Rādhā, sowing many arrows as he came.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣāv api tadā yudhāmanyūttamaujasau dhanaṃjayarathaṃ hitvā rādheyaṃ pratyudīyayuḥ
english: Then too the two wheel-guards, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, leaving Dhanaṃjaya's chariot, advanced against the son of Rādhā.

sanskrit: rādheyo 'pi mahārāja śaravarṣaṃ samutsṛjan abhyadravat susaṃkruddho raṇe śaineyam acyutam
english: The son of Rādhā too, O great king, loosing a downpour of arrows, in high fury charged the steadfast grandson of Śini in the fight.

sanskrit: naiva daivaṃ na gāndharvaṃ nāsuroragarākṣasam tādṛśaṃ bhuvi vā yuddhaṃ divi vā śrutam ity uta
english: No such battle, of gods or gandharvas, of asuras, serpents, or rākṣasas, was ever heard of, whether on earth or in heaven.

sanskrit: upāramata tat sainyaṃ sarathāśvanaradvipam tayor dṛṣṭvā mahārāja karma saṃmūḍhacetanam
english: That host, with its chariots, horses, men, and elephants, stood still, O great king, its senses bewildered at beholding the feats of those two.

sanskrit: sarve ca samapaśyanta tad yuddham atimānuṣam tayor nṛvarayo rājan sārathyaṃ dārukasya ca
english: And all gazed upon that superhuman combat of those two foremost of men, O king, and upon the charioteering of Dāruka.

sanskrit: gatapratyāgatāvṛttair maṇḍalaiḥ saṃnivartanaiḥ sārathes tu rathasthasya kāśyapeyasya vismitāḥ
english: They marveled at the son of Kaśyapa as he stood at his post, with his goings forth and returnings, his wheelings and his turnings about.

sanskrit: nabhastalagatāś caiva devagandharvadānavāḥ atīvāvahitā draṣṭuṃ karṇaśaineyayo raṇam
english: And the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas in the vault of heaven were most intent to behold the battle of Karṇa and the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: mitrārthe tau parākrāntau spardhinau śuṣmiṇau raṇe karṇaś cāmarasaṃkāśo yuyudhānaś ca sātyakiḥ
english: For their friends' sake the two strove on, rivals fierce and mettlesome in the fray — Karṇa, like an immortal, and Yuyudhāna, the son of Sātyaka.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ tau mahārāja śaravarṣair avarṣatām pramamātha śineḥ pautraṃ karṇaḥ sāyakavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Each upon the other, O great king, they rained their showers of arrows; and Karṇa battered the grandson of Śini with floods of shafts.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇo nidhanaṃ kauravyajalasaṃdhayoḥ karṇaḥ śokasamāviṣṭo mahoraga iva śvasan
english: Unable to brook the slaying of the Kaurava and of Jalasaṃdha, Karṇa, filled with grief, hissed like a great serpent.

sanskrit: sa śaineyaṃ raṇe kruddhaḥ pradahann iva cakṣuṣā abhyadravata vegena punaḥ punar ariṃdamaḥ
english: That tamer of foes, enraged, as if consuming the grandson of Śini with his very gaze, charged him again and again with vehemence in the fray.

sanskrit: taṃ tu saṃprekṣya saṃkruddhaṃ sātyakiḥ pratyavidhyata mahatā śaravarṣeṇa gajaḥ pratigajaṃ yathā
english: But beholding him in his wrath, Sātyaki pierced him back with a mighty downpour of arrows, as one elephant withstands another.

sanskrit: tau sametya naravyāghrau vyāghrāv iva tarasvinau anyonyaṃ saṃtatakṣāte raṇe 'nupamavikramau
english: Those two tigers among men, closing like swift and tireless tigers, hewed at each other in the battle, peerless in prowess.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaṃ śineḥ pautraḥ sarvapāraśavaiḥ śaraiḥ bibheda sarvagātreṣu punaḥ punar ariṃdamaḥ
english: Then the grandson of Śini, that tamer of foes, pierced Karṇa in every limb, again and again, with shafts all wrought of iron.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena rathanīḍād apāharat aśvāṃś ca caturaḥ śvetān nijaghne niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: With a broad-headed arrow he swept his charioteer from the chariot-box, and with whetted shafts he slew his four white steeds.

sanskrit: chittvā dhvajaṃ śatenaiva śatadhā puruṣarṣabhaḥ cakāra virathaṃ karṇaṃ tava putrasya paśyataḥ
english: Cleaving his banner a hundredfold with a hundred arrows, that bull among men left Karṇa without a car, before the very eyes of your son.

sanskrit: tato vimanaso rājaṃs tāvakāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ vṛṣasenaḥ karṇasutaḥ śalyo madrādhipas tathā
english: Then your bulls among men were dismayed, O king — Vṛṣasena, the son of Karṇa, and Śalya, the lord of the Madras,

sanskrit: droṇaputraś ca śaineyaṃ sarvataḥ paryavārayan tataḥ paryākulaṃ sarvaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: and the son of Droṇa — they surrounded the grandson of Śini on every side; thereupon all became a tumult, and nothing could be discerned.

sanskrit: tathā sātyakinā vīre virathe sūtaje kṛte hāhākāras tato rājan sarvasainyeṣu cābhavat
english: When the heroic son of the sūta had thus been left carless by Sātyaki, a cry of dismay arose, O king, throughout all the armies.

sanskrit: karṇo 'pi vihvalo rājan sātvatenārditaḥ śaraiḥ duryodhanarathaṃ rājann āruroha viniḥśvasan
english: And Karṇa too, reeling, O king, tormented by the Sātvata's arrows, mounted Duryodhana's chariot, breathing hard.

sanskrit: mānayaṃs tava putrasya bālyāt prabhṛti sauhṛdam kṛtāṃ rājyapradānena pratijñāṃ paripālayan
english: Honoring the friendship he had borne your son from boyhood, and keeping the vow he had made when granted the kingdom,

sanskrit: tathā tu virathe karṇe putrān vai tava pārthiva duḥśāsanamukhāñ śūrān nāvadhīt sātyakir vaśī
english: even with Karṇa thus carless, the self-controlled Sātyaki did not slay your heroic sons, O king, with Duḥśāsana at their head.

sanskrit: rakṣan pratijñāṃ ca punar bhīmasenakṛtāṃ purā virathān vihvalāṃś cakre na tu prāṇair vyayojayat
english: Guarding too the vow Bhīmasena had once made of old, he made them carless and reeling, yet did not part them from their lives.

sanskrit: bhīmasenena tu vadhaḥ putrāṇāṃ te pratiśrutaḥ punardyūte ca pārthena vadhaḥ karṇasya śaṃśrutaḥ
english: For the slaying of your sons had been pledged by Bhīmasena, and at the second dicing the slaying of Karṇa had been vowed by Pārtha.

sanskrit: vadhe tv akurvan yatnaṃ te tasya karṇamukhās tadā nāśaknuvaṃś ca taṃ hantuṃ sātyakiṃ pravarā rathāḥ
english: Though they made every effort then to slay him, those foremost chariot-warriors with Karṇa at their head were unable to slay that Sātyaki.

sanskrit: drauṇiś ca kṛtavarmā ca tathaivānye mahārathāḥ nirjitā dhanuṣaikena śataśaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ kāṅkṣatā paralokaṃ ca dharmarājasya ca priyam
english: The son of Droṇa, and Kṛtavarman, and likewise other great chariot-warriors — bulls among the kṣatriyas by the hundred — were vanquished with a single bow by one who sought the other world and the favor of the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇayoḥ sadṛśo vīrye sātyakiḥ śatrukarśanaḥ kṛṣṇo vāpi bhavel loke pārtho vāpi dhanurdharaḥ śaineyo vā naravyāghraś caturtho nopalabhyate
english: Sātyaki, scourge of his foes, was equal in valor to the two Kṛṣṇas; in the world there is Kṛṣṇa, or Pārtha the bowman, or the grandson of Śini, that tiger among men — a fourth such is not to be found.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ajayyaṃ ratham āsthāya vāsudevasya sātyakiḥ virathaṃ kṛtavān karṇaṃ vāsudevasamo yuvā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Mounting the unconquerable chariot of Vāsudeva, the youthful Sātyaki, the peer of Vāsudeva, left Karṇa without a car —

sanskrit: dārukeṇa samāyuktaṃ svabāhubaladarpitaḥ kaccid anyaṃ samārūḍhaḥ sa rathaṃ sātyakiḥ punaḥ
english: the car driven by Dāruka — proud of the strength of his own arms. Did Sātyaki then mount yet another chariot of his own?

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ kuśalo hy asi bhāṣitum asahyaṃ tam ahaṃ manye tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: This I wish to hear, for you are skilled in the telling; I deem him irresistible — tell me of it, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan yathā tasya ratham anyaṃ mahāmatiḥ dārukasyānujas tūrṇaṃ kalpanāvidhikalpitam
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, how the wise younger brother of Dāruka swiftly made ready for him another chariot, fashioned with every proper appointment —

sanskrit: āyasaiḥ kāñcanaiś cāpi paṭṭair naddhaṃ sakūbaram tārāsahasrakhacitaṃ siṃhadhvajapatākinam
english: bound with bands of iron and of gold, fitted with its pole, studded with a thousand stars, bearing a banner and pennon marked with a lion.

sanskrit: aśvair vātajavair yuktaṃ hemabhāṇḍaparicchadaiḥ pāṇḍurair indusaṃkāśaiḥ sarvaśabdātigair dṛḍhaiḥ
english: It was yoked with horses swift as the wind, caparisoned with golden trappings, white and bright as the moon, hardy, and heedless of every clamor.

sanskrit: citrakāñcanasaṃnāhair vājimukhyair viśāṃ pate ghaṇṭājālākularavaṃ śaktitomaravidyutam
english: With foremost steeds in armor of variegated gold, O lord of peoples — a chariot loud with the ringing of clustered bells, flashing with lances and javelins —

sanskrit: vṛtaṃ sāṃgrāmikair dravyair bahuśastraparicchadam rathaṃ saṃpādayām āsa meghagambhīranisvanam
english: furnished with all the gear of war, abounding in many weapons — such a chariot, deep-voiced as a thundercloud, he made ready.

sanskrit: taṃ samāruhya śaineyas tava sainyam upādravat dāruko 'pi yathākāmaṃ prayayau keśavāntikam
english: Mounting it, the grandson of Śini fell upon your host; and Dāruka, as he pleased, went off to the side of Keśava.

sanskrit: karṇasyāpi mahārāja śaṅkhagokṣīrapāṇḍuraiḥ citrakāñcanasaṃnāhaiḥ sadaśvair vegavattaraiḥ
english: For Karṇa too, O great king, they brought up a chariot — drawn by goodly steeds, swifter still, white as the conch and as cow's milk, clad in armor of variegated gold,

sanskrit: hemakakṣyādhvajopetaṃ kḷptayantrapatākinam agryaṃ rathaṃ suyantāraṃ bahuśastraparicchadam
english: furnished with girths of gold and with a banner, decked with well-wrought gear and pennon, a peerless car with a good driver, abounding in many weapons.

sanskrit: upājahrus tam āsthāya karṇo 'py abhyadravad ripūn etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: This they brought up, and mounting it Karṇa too charged upon his foes. All this have I told you, even as you asked of me.

sanskrit: bhūyaś cāpi nibodha tvaṃ tavāpanayajaṃ kṣayam ekatriṃśat tava sutā bhīmasenena pātitāḥ
english: Now learn further of the ruin born of your own misrule: one-and-thirty of your sons have been struck down by Bhīmasena,

sanskrit: durmukhaṃ pramukhe kṛtvā satataṃ citrayodhinam śataśo nihatāḥ śūrāḥ sātvatenārjunena ca
english: with Durmukha, that ever-skillful and wondrous fighter, at their head; and heroes by the hundred have been slain by the Sātvata and by Arjuna.
